text:
jin: runtime-detector flagged an anomalous exec: /bin/sh spawned from pod `batch-worker-5` on prod-3, looks like host namespace interaction. tagging @oncall @devsecops
ops-bot: ALERT: runtime anomaly detected for pod=batch-worker-5 node=prod-3 type=HOST_NS_EXEC severity=high
oncall: I'm online, investigating now
jin: quick paste from containerd logs:
```
Apr 12 02:12:58 prod-3 kernel: audit: type=1300 msg=audit:... pid=4321 exe=/usr/bin/sh
containerd[1234]: exec: "/bin/sh" args:["/bin/sh" "-c" "..."] uid=0 gid=0
```
michael: can we cordon prod-3-node06? i'll take it out of rotation and do a live snapshot
oncall: cordon+drain kicked off: `kubectl cordon prod-3-node06 && kubectl drain prod-3-node06 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
elaine: pod spec shows a hostPath and hostPID: here's the relevant snippet:
```
containers:
  - name: worker
    image: registry.internal/build-worker:latest
    securityContext:
      privileged: true
    volumeMounts:
      - mountPath: /var/run/docker.sock
        name: dockersock
hostPID: true
volumes:
  - name: dockersock
    hostPath:
      path: /var/run/docker.sock
```
sara: that image digest doesn't match our registry snapshot. `registry.internal/build-worker:latest` pulled on node shows sha256:deadbeef != expected sha256:cafef00d. could be tampering or a compromised pipeline artifact
devsecops: containment steps: 1) kill pod 2) cordon node (done) 3) snapshot /var/log/pods, /var/log/containers and containerd state 4) preserve node disk and memory if possible 5) revoke CI SA tokens and suspend CI run triggers
jin: `kubectl get events` didn't show kubectl exec entries. checking kube-audit logs now — there is a `create` of a privileged pod by `system:serviceaccount:ci:deployer` at 02:11:56 UTC. suspicious token use
michael: rotate the `ci:deployer` SA token now, revoke any long-lived kubeconfigs held in CI. i'll start node forensic collection and upload to secure bucket
devsecops: also check registry access logs for pushed manifests/tags around 02:00-03:00 UTC. if image digest changed, we need to know when and by which actor. enable read-only access to registry for forensics
elaine: i killed the pod and blocked outbound egress from the node to registries. have we alerted legal/comms?
oncall: paging daphne from secops now. filing incident ticket INF-2026-045 and bridging to #incidents. No external customer impact detected so far — SLA checks running
jin: root causes to investigate: (A) SA token misuse / RBAC over-permissive in ci namespace, (B) hostPath/privileged containers allowed in workload manifests, (C) unsigned images allowed to run. immediate mitigations: rotate SA tokens, block hostPath/hostPID in admission controller, require image digests in deployments, add image signature verification (cosign)
sara: agree. followups: add pipeline step to pin digests and publish SBOMs. require `imagePullPolicy` strictness and disallow `:latest` in prod manifests
devsecops: long-term: enforce OPA/Gatekeeper policy that denies hostPID/hostNetwork/privileged and requires cosign verification. increase audit log retention and export to secure ledger (immutable store). consider monthly KMS key rotation for image signing keys and rotation on suspected compromise
ops-bot: Incident INF-2026-045 created by jin. bridged to #incidents and pager oncall lists updated
michael: uploading forensic artifacts to secure bucket: gs://redwood-forensics/INF-2026-045/prod-3-node06-2026-04-12.tar.gz (owner=michael), checksum sha256:ab12...
jin: assigning owners/next actions: michael=forensics, elaine=registry audit, sara=CI hardening, jin=admission policies & RBAC PRs, devsecops=incident writeup and postmortem. ETA for mitigations: 48 hours. will post timeline and exec summary to #all-hands-security later
sara: :thumbsup: please include checklist for emergency KMS rotate and contact list for compliance/legal
devsecops: creating post-incident document template now and will attach logs/artifacts to INF-2026-045. thanks team
jin: thanks everyone. closing triage for now, will update when we've got forensic analysis and PR links
